question: Can Muslims shop at the markets and take advantage of sales on non-Muslim religious holidays?
answer:
As for taking advantage of other things going on, I'll just add some other stuff here as well. How about going to the bazaars on the day of their Eids? How about going to their shopping malls and taking advantage of sales? How about that?

Imam Ahmad was asked about going to the bazaar on the day of the Christian celebrations. And by the way, in all civilizations the bazaars have extra on the days of celebration. This is human culture, correct? It's human culture. When you're in India, Diwali, the bazaars are doing that. When you're in the Zoroastrian places, Nauruz. When you're in these lands, Thanksgiving. This is human nature. When you're in Pakistan, the days of Eid: buy one get three free in Pakistan every time, and then you still bargain for the fourth one free. Anyway, the point being that it's human nature: where there is a holy day, there are going to be bazaars that are offering concessions.

Imam Ahmad was asked, "Can we go to the bazaars of the Christians on their holy days?" And he said if he is going to the bazaar and he doesn't go to the church, that is not a problem. And Imam Ahmad was on the stricter side of the madhahib in this, but even he's like, what's the big deal? You're going to the bazaar, you're taking advantage of the shopping, you're not getting involved in the worship, you're not going to the church on the holy day.

And even Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, who generally speaking is one of the strictest 'ulama when it comes to celebrations, and I have no problem with that opinion, but do realize there are other opinions, as I'm going to mention: even Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah was asked about buying on the holy days of the Christians and whatnot, and he said, no problem, you can purchase from them on their holy days. But he did add: you should not sell to them things that they're going to use for their festivals. So if they're going to do something that's going to be in their worshipping other than Allah, you should not sell it to them.

So that's with regards to taking advantage of sales and whatnot: **no problem.**
